paragraphs.title: Political Deceit and the Lord’s Dispute with Israel

easy.explanation: Hosea says, “Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind.”
easy.q: What does Ephraim feed on and follow after?

easy.explanation: Ephraim made a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil was carried into Egypt.
easy.q: With which nations did Ephraim make a covenant or maintain contact?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “The LORD hath also a controversy with Judah.”
easy.q: With whom does the LORD also have a controversy?

medium.explanation: Ephraim sought political relationships with both Assyria and Egypt rather than trusting the LORD.
medium.q: What do Ephraim’s dealings with Assyria and Egypt suggest?

medium.explanation: The LORD promises to punish Jacob according to his ways and recompense him according to his doings.
medium.q: What does “according to his ways” mean in verse 2?

answers: They are judged according to their deeds
They are judged by their wealth
medium.explanation: Both references emphasize that the LORD responds to a people according to its conduct.
medium.q: What common principle applies to Jacob and Judah in these verses?

challenge.explanation: Ephraim increases lies and desolation while making covenants with Assyria and Egypt.
challenge.q: Which description best summarizes Ephraim’s behavior?

answers: Judah is also accountable to the LORD
Judah is unrelated to Israel’s history
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s controversy includes Judah, showing that Judah too will answer for its ways.
challenge.q: Why is Judah mentioned alongside Jacob?

answers: The deeds described bring corresponding judgment
challenge.explanation: The false and destructive conduct of Ephraim is the kind of doing for which recompense is promised.
challenge.q: How do “lies and desolation” relate to “his doings”?

paragraphs.title: Jacob as a Model of Struggle and Attachment to God

easy.explanation: The passage says Jacob had power with God and prevailed over the angel.
easy.q: With whom did Jacob have power?

easy.explanation: The text says, “he found him in Bethel, and there he spake with us.”
easy.q: Where did Jacob find the angel and speak with him?

easy.explanation: The command is, “Therefore turn thou to thy God.”
easy.q: To whom are the people told to return?

answers: Keep mercy, keep judgment, and wait on God continually
Seek wealth, make alliances, and increase trade
Offer violence, pursue power, and trust Egypt
medium.explanation: Verse 6 commands Israel to keep mercy and judgment and wait on God continually.
medium.q: What three responses are commanded after returning to God?

medium.explanation: Jacob wrestled, wept, made supplication, and prevailed over the angel.
medium.q: What does “prevailed” mean in the account of Jacob?

answers: It presents struggle joined with prayer and perseverance
It teaches dependence on foreign powers
It portrays Jacob as abandoning God
medium.explanation: Jacob’s struggle, tears, and supplication provide a pattern of persistent dependence on God.
medium.q: How does Jacob’s experience support the call to return to God?

answers: His victory depended only on physical strength
challenge.explanation: Jacob’s encounter is described not merely as a physical struggle but also as an act of pleading.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the words “he wept, and made supplication”?

answers: It recalls an encounter with God that supports the call to return
It is presented as a center of foreign trade
It replaces the need to obey God
challenge.explanation: Bethel is associated with Jacob’s encounter and speech with God, followed by the call to return to Him.
challenge.q: How does Bethel function in the passage?

answers: Struggle, supplication, and continual dependence on God
challenge.explanation: Jacob’s example combines perseverance, prayer, and reliance upon God.
challenge.q: What model does Jacob provide for Israel?

paragraphs.title: Oppression, Arrogance, and the Promise of Restoration

easy.explanation: The merchant is described as having “the balances of deceit” in his hand.
easy.q: What does the merchant have in his hand?

easy.explanation: Ephraim says, “Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance.”
easy.q: What does Ephraim claim to have become?

answers: That He was Israel’s God from the land of Egypt
easy.explanation: The LORD identifies Himself as Israel’s God from the land of Egypt.
easy.q: What does the LORD recall about Israel’s past?

answers: That no iniquity or sin will be found in them
That they were acts of mercy
That they were performed by prophets
medium.explanation: Ephraim claims, “In all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me that were sin.”
medium.q: What does Ephraim claim about his labours?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes dishonest commercial practices and oppression.

answers: He uses prosperity to deny the wrongdoing evident in his conduct
He gives away all his possessions
He asks the prophet to defend him
medium.explanation: Ephraim boasts of wealth while denying sin, even though the merchant is characterized by deceit and oppression.
medium.q: What contrast appears between Ephraim’s wealth and his claim of innocence?

answers: He claims innocence while being associated with deceit and oppression
He claims poverty while being generous
He claims to be a prophet while serving God
challenge.explanation: Ephraim denies iniquity, but the surrounding description portrays dishonest and oppressive behavior.
challenge.q: What contradiction is exposed in Ephraim’s words?

answers: By refusing to speak to Israel
challenge.explanation: The LORD says He spoke by the prophets, multiplied visions, and used similitudes.
challenge.q: How did the LORD communicate with Israel according to these verses?

answers: A promise to restore Israel to a time of remembered divine care
That the Exodus was Israel’s sin
challenge.explanation: The LORD recalls His care from Egypt and promises to make Israel dwell in tabernacles as in the days of the solemn feast.
challenge.q: What does the reference to tabernacles and the solemn feast suggest?

paragraphs.title: Jacob, the Exodus, and Ephraim’s Accountability

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Jacob fled into the country of Syria.”
The passage says, “by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt.”
easy.q: By whom did the LORD bring Israel out of Egypt?

answers: The king of Egypt to mercy
easy.explanation: Ephraim is said to have provoked the LORD to anger most bitterly.

answers: Both are described in connection with service, exile, and preservation
medium.explanation: Jacob served for a wife in Syria, while Israel was brought from Egypt and preserved through a prophet.
medium.q: What parallel connects Jacob and Israel in this passage?

answers: Jacob’s labor while serving for a wife
medium.explanation: The verse explains that Jacob served for a wife by keeping sheep.
medium.q: What does “for a wife he kept sheep” describe?

answers: The prophet was an instrument of deliverance and preservation
The prophet made a covenant with Assyria
medium.explanation: A prophet was used both to bring Israel out of Egypt and to preserve Israel.
medium.q: What role did the prophet have in Israel’s history?

answers: To connect the ancestor’s story with Israel’s national history
To present Jacob as the ruler of Egypt
To explain Ephraim’s alliance with Assyria
challenge.explanation: The passage links Jacob’s service in Syria with Israel’s deliverance from Egypt.
challenge.q: Why are Jacob and the Exodus mentioned together?

answers: He will bear the consequences of provoking the LORD
challenge.explanation: Ephraim’s anger-provoking conduct results in his blood and reproach being returned upon him.
challenge.q: What does the ending teach about Ephraim’s responsibility?

answers: The passage moves from divine deliverance to human accountability
The passage moves from wealth to commercial success
The passage moves from Assyria to praise for Ephraim
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s saving action is recalled, but Ephraim is still held accountable for provoking Him.
challenge.q: What development appears between the Exodus reference and the final judgment?
